KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r1.claim: The passage's surface meaning indicates Abraham's people worshipped the moon, sun, and stars, or idols that represented them on earth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r1.anchor: Hz. İbrâhim’in kavmi ay, güneş ve yıldızlara veya bunların yerdeki sembolü olan putlara tapıyorlardı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r2.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r2.claim: Their greatest heavenly god was the sun, and their greatest earthly god was Baal, its representative idol.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r2.anchor: gökyüzündeki en büyük tanrıları güneş, yeryüzündeki en büyük tanrıları ise onun temsilcisi olan Baal adındaki put idi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r3.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r3.claim: They believed idols governed human life and that time brought about creation and destruction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:70/r3.anchor: insanların hayatını putlar yönetiyordu, yaratma ve yok etme işini de zaman yapıyordu (İbn Âşûr, XIX, 141).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative, like the preceding anecdote, serves the same preaching purpose and also ends with the recurring verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.anchor: the purpose of narrating this anecdote is the same as the one intended for the previous one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.claim: The Abraham account fills the gap after Noah in the previous sūrah because Abraham was the most prominent messenger between Noah and Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.anchor: the most prominent messenger between Noah (sws) and Moses (sws) was Abraham (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r2.claim: The question expresses amazement and distaste at the baseless idols Abraham’s people worshipped.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r2.anchor: amazement and distaste pointing to the baselessness of idols Abraham’s (sws) nation was worshipping.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r3.claim: Idols are Satan’s lures; Satan is mankind’s eternal enemy whose mission is to keep people from the straight path.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p421/r3.anchor: They are lures of Satan and Satan is an eternal enemy of mankind. His real mission is to stop people from going to the straight path.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r5.claim: Calling the fathers الأقدمون stresses how long idol worship had persisted, reaching back to Noah’s time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r5.anchor: وآباؤكم الأقدمون: وصفهم بالأقدمين دلالة على ما تقادم عبادة الأصنام فيهم، وإذ كانوا قد عبدوها في زمان نوح عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#5/r1.claim: Abraham's address is a rebuke that declares the idols and their worship false; the fact that the error is ancient only makes its longstanding falsehood clearer.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#5/r1.anchor: والكلام انكار وتوبيخ يتضمن بطلان آلهتهم وعبادتها وأن عبادتها ضلال قديم لافائدة في قدمه الا ظهور بطلانه كما يؤذن بهذا وصف آبائهم بالأقدمين

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r5.claim: Ancient practice does not establish correctness, and falsehood does not become truth through age.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r5.anchor: فإن التقدم لا يدل على الصحة ولا ينقلب به الباطل حقا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r7.claim: Abraham pushes their imitation to its limit: precedence is no proof, and age cannot turn falsehood into truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r7.anchor: فإن التقدم والأولوية لا تكون برهانا على الصحة , والباطل لا ينقلب حقا بالقدمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p141/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p141/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p141/r3.claim: Adding the fathers to the address underscores Ibrahim’s lack of concern for idols and invalidates ancestral worship as proof of their right to worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p141/r3.anchor: وعطف { آباؤكم } على { أنتم } لزيادة إظهار قلة اكتراثه بتلك الأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p141/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p141/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p141/r4.claim: Calling the ancestors ancient intensifies the rebuke of imitation, since communities ordinarily regard older ancestors as stronger precedent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p141/r4.anchor: ووصف الآباء بالأقدمية إيغال في قلة الاكتراث بتقليدهم لأن عرف الأمم أن الآباء كلما تقادم عهدهم كان تقليدهم آكد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r5.claim: Abraham challenges the idols to harm him if they have power, declaring himself their enemy and unconcerned by them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r5.anchor: فلتخلص إلي بالمساءة، فإني عدو لها لا أباليها ولا أفكر فيها.

MUQATIL:26:69-85/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r5.claim: They defend worship by saying they found their fathers doing it; Abraham then asks about the idols worshipped by them and their earliest ancestors.
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r5.anchor: يعنى هكذا يعبدون الأصنام { قال } إبراهيم:

QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r13.claim: الأقدمون means the earlier, first ancestors.

RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r12.claim: Abraham’s reply teaches that falsehood does not become true by being old or new, or by having many or few adherents.
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r12.anchor: أن الباطل لا يتغير بأن يكون قديما أو حديثا ، ولا بأن يكون في فاعلية كثرة أو قلة

STUDYQURAN:26:74/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r3.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r3.claim: Abraham's answer shows that an error remains wrong whether recent or entrenched, regardless of the authority invoked for it.
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r3.anchor: Abraham’s reply shows that error, whether recent or entrenched, is error regardless of the authority to which one defers in upholding it

STUDYQURAN:26:74/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r4.claim: The source links this rejection of ancestral imitation to 5:104 and similar injunctions in 7:28, 10:78, 28:36, 31:21, and 43:24.
STUDYQURAN:26:74/r4.anchor: For the notion of idolaters blindly following the ways of their forefathers, see commentary on 5:104

TAB-FULL:v17p591/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p591/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p591/r1.claim: “The most ancient” means the earlier generations before the people Abraham addressed, who also worshipped idols.
TAB-FULL:v17p591/r1.anchor: الذين كان إبراهيم يخاطبهم، وهم الأولون قبلهم ممن كان على مثل ما كان عليه الذين كلمهم إبراهيم من عبادة الأصنام

TAB-FULL:v17p591/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p591/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p591/r2.claim: The idols will be Abraham's enemies on Judgment Day if he worships them, as other scripture says false gods will disown their worshippers and oppose them.
TAB-FULL:v17p591/r2.anchor: فإن معنى ذلك: فإنهم عدو لي لو عبدتهم يوم القيامة، كما قال جل ثناؤه {واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة ليكونوا لهم عزا

TABRISI:26:72-77/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:72-77/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:72-77/r15.claim: Abraham's challenge concerns the idols worshipped by the people and their earliest ancestors; كان appears because the statement combines the present with the past.
TABRISI:26:72-77/r15.anchor: أي والذين كان آباؤكم يعبدونهم وإنما دخل لفظة كان لأنه جمع بين الحال والماضي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p65#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p65#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p65#2/r1.claim: The earliest ancestors are the people of the distant past.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads Abraham's words as saying that his people and their ancestors are his enemies, except ancestors who worshipped the Lord of the worlds.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r1.anchor: فإنه ليس لي بعدو وهذا تفسير الحسن.
